12700 Norwalk Boulevard. The agenda for the special meeting is as follows:

   City Council Agenda Report
  May 31, 2025

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Jana Stuard, Director of Finance/City Treasurer

SUBJECT:  FISCAL YEAR 2025/26 PROPOSED BUDGET

Background:

Each year the City is required by the Norwalk Municipal Code to prepare an annual budget and
present it to City Council for public consideration. The proposed budget for the upcoming fiscal
year, which covers the period July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, was distributed to the members of
City Council on May 22, 2025 and presented to the Finance Ad Hoc Committee on May 27. The
document was also made available for public review in the City Clerk’s Department and on the
City’s web page.

The Fiscal Year (FY) 2025/26 Proposed Budget contains the following sections:
  Budget Summaries:
  ✓ Changes to Fund Balances/Working Capital
  ✓ Inter-Fund Transfers
  ✓ All Funds – Expenditure Summary
  ✓ All Funds – Full Time Positions and Part Time Hours
  ✓ General Fund Revenue Summary
  ✓ General Fund Expenditure Summaries by Type and Function
  Revenues – all funds
  Capital Outlays
  Capital Projects – carryover and new projects.
  Department Summaries – contains the following information for each departmental
  division (Budget Unit):
  ✓ Organizational Chart – represents organizational structure of each department
  ✓ Personnel Information – summarizes budgeted full-time positions and part-time
  hours.
  ✓ Activities and Objectives

Fiscal Year 2025/26 Proposed Budget  Page No. 2

  ✓ Activity Detail – contains the explanation and/or the breakdown of certain
  expenditure line items, such as contract services, membership, special studies,
  special projects, etc.
  ✓ Departmental Expenditure Budget – details line items per Budget Unit.

The FY 2025/26 Budget has been prepared in an economic environment of uncertainty and is
balanced by using the City’s available resources, including the Pension Stabilization Trust Fund,
which for the first time from its inception will be used to offset the cost of the required Unfunded
Accrued Liability annual contribution to the California Public Employees’ Retirement System
(CalPERS). The available General Fund balance is used to replenish the City’s capital reserves
for the Vehicle Equipment Replacement, Parks Renovation, and Street Renovation funds.

Subsequent to City Council direction at this and following budget review meetings, a final budget
will be prepared and submitted for adoption at a public hearing scheduled for a meeting in June.

Fiscal Impact:

Contingent on City Council’s direction, the proposed budget, when adopted, will serve as the
City’s expenditure plan for a one-year period, covering July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

Citizens Advised:

Draft Budget on file in the City Clerk’s Department and published on the City’s web page, at:
https://www.norwalk.org/departments_services/finance/budget_and_financial_reports/index.php

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 3: Create and sustain resilient
and economically prosperous community.

Recommended Action:

The Fiscal Year 2025/26 Proposed Budget is presented for discussion and direction.

SUBJECT:  REPORT ON 2024 ACTIVITY OF CITY OF NORWALK'S ADVISORY BODIES

Background:

In order to determine whether new advisory bodies should be added to the City’s roster, the City
Council requested an overview of the current advisory bodies’ activity over calendar year 2024,
focusing specifically on the vacancy rates of its members, the frequency of the meetings, and
reasons for missed meetings.

Art in Public Places Committee
The Art in Public Places Committee is tasked with reviewing art projects submitted as part of the
Art in Public Places Program to ensure their compliance with all City Council criteria. The staff
liaison is Theresa Devoy. Its FY2025 budget is $301,500. It held three special meetings in 2024,
as it meets only when there is business to discuss. It had three vacant seats out of 10 in January,
and then four vacant seats for the remainder of the year.

Senior Commission
The Senior Commission promotes communication and cooperation among all patrons of the
Senior Center, provides a forum which encourages discussion and resolution of concerns related
to senor programs offered by the City, as well as issues and needs pertaining to older adults in
the community. The staff liaison is Gabriela Regalado. Its FY2025 budget is $800. It met nine
out of 12 months. It did not hold any meetings for the months of July, August and December. The
meetings in July and August were cancelled for summer break, and the December meeting was
cancelled due to the holidays. The Commission had one vacant seat out of five through October,
and full staff for the rest of year.

Community Promotion Commission
The Community Promotion Commission promotes community and City activities, events,
programs and services. The staff liaison is Levy Sun. Its budget for fiscal year (FY) 2025 is
$20,200. The Community Promotion Commission met nearly every month for calendar year

special meeting was held in December to make up for the lack of quorum meeting. There was

the remainder of the year.

Historical Heritage Commission
The Historical Heritage Commission was formed in 1959 with the intention of preserving
Norwalk’s rich history. It is responsible for research and documentation of the City’s past.
Members of the Commission also serve as docents at Norwalk’s Hargitt House Museum. The
staff liaison is Pati Escano. Its FY2025 budget is $1,000. It met nine out of 12 months. The
November meeting was cancelled due to lack of quorum and the May and December meetings
were cancelled due to the holidays. For the first three months of 2024, the Commission had three
vacant seats out of 10. They had four vacant seats April through August, and five seats remained
vacant for the remainder of the year.

International Friendship Commission
The International Friendship Commission is meant to provide input on the City’s Sister City
programs. The staff liaison is Amber Bulosan. It has a budget of $5,000. Unfortunately, it had no
members from January 2024 through July 2024. One commissioner was added in August and
another in October. It ended the year with three vacant seats out of five. It did not hold any
meetings in 2024 due to lack of quorum.

Parks and Recreation Commission
The Parks and Recreation Commission provides input regarding the programs, activities and
issues relating to recreation, cultural arts and overall community events. The staff liaison is Allan
Perdomo. Its FY2025 budget is $1,000. It met almost every month in 2024, cancelling only
December for the holiday season. It had one vacant seat for the month of January, but was fully
staffed for the rest of the year beginning in February.

Planning Commission
The Planning Commission carries out functions mandated by State law. It considers a wide
variety of matters to fulfill its functions, including conducting public hearings for all General Plan
amendments, zone changes, conditional use permits, zone variances, and text amendments.
The Commission also reviews and acts on a number of other applications for development,
review design criteria and standards on development proposals, and considers appeals of
administrative decisions. Lastly, the members also form the Property Maintenance and
Rehabilitation Appeals Board, which meets annually. Its FY2025 budget is $19,750. It met six
out of 12 months. For the months of February, April, May, August, and September, it did not meet
due to lack of business. The December special meeting was cancelled due to lack of quorum.
The Planning Commission had no vacant seats for the first five months of the year. In June, July
and August the Planning Commission had one vacant seat. In September, the Commission
returned to being fully staffed and remained that way for the rest of 2024.

Public Safety Commission
The Public Safety Commission addresses public safety issues, including traffic safety, parking
control, emergency preparedness, and the enforcement and enhancement of the Norwalk
Municipal Code. It reviews concerns brought before it and makes specific recommendations for
improvement to City Council. It also serves as a resource through which citizens can voice their
public safety issues and have these concerns addressed. The staff liaison is Richard Newton. Its
FY2025 budget is $1,000. The Commission met eight out of 12 months. It did not hold any
meetings in the months of January, February, September, and October for a variety of reasons.
In January and September, it cancelled meetings due to the corresponding holidays. In February,
they were unable to meet due to inclement weather. Lastly, the October meeting was cancelled
due to the staff liaison being unavailable. The Public Safety Commission had one vacant seat
from January to June, July they were fully staffed, and August through the remainder of the year
there was one vacant seat out of 10.

Social Services Commission
The Social Services Commission provides input on social services-related issues and assists
with promotion of the Social Services Department’s activities and special events. The staff liaison
is Gabriela Regalado. Its FY2025 budget is $500. It met eight out of 12 months. In March, the
meeting was cancelled due to the meeting location being needed as a voting center. In May, they
lacked quorum. For June and July, they cancelled for summer break. The Commission had full
staff January through June, only one vacant seat out of 10 in July and August, was fully staffed
from September through November, and had two vacant seats in December.

Youth Commission
The Youth Commission is meant to provide the City Council with recommendations from the
youth of Norwalk regarding City programs, special events, and ideas to help shape development
opportunities with the City. The staff liaison is Rosie Lozoya. It has a budget of $2,000.
Unfortunately, the Youth Commission was vacant for all of 2024.
